processing: An unoxidised green tea shaped into fine strands, as with other maojian; the finer detail of its method is little documented.
harvest_season: Spring, as is usual for maojian-style greens, with the earliest tender pickings most valued.
appearance_dry: Fine, slender strands of a bright jade green.
taste_profile: A clear, high aroma with a fresh, mellow taste, a rich body and a sweet aftertaste.

brewing.notes: Typical handling for fine maojian: water off the boil and a short first steep.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year green tea, mainly spring picking, as is usual for the class, and best within about a year. Caihua Maojian is also a commercial brand name in Wufeng, so check who made the lot.
description:
Caihua Maojian is a green tea from Caihua township in the west of Wufeng Tujia Autonomous County, in the Yichang area of Hubei. It is promoted as a flagship Hubei green, from a county historically tied to black tea.

The leaf is made into fine, slender strands of a bright jade green, typical of the maojian style. Little has been written about any step particular to this tea, so assume the usual maojian method of fixing, rolling and drying.

It is summed up as clear in fragrance, green in the cup, mellow in taste and rich in body. Treat it gently, like other fine strand greens, and it should stay fresh with a sweet aftertaste.

When buying, the name often appears with a company attached, since a Wufeng firm trades under it. Ask for this year's harvest, and expect a clean, even leaf rather than broken bits.
history: Wufeng's tea-making has a long background: the county lies in the old Xiazhou area mentioned in Lu Yu's Classic of Tea, and it later became a home of Yihong black tea. The name Caihua Maojian itself is modern, and some accounts date its creation to the 1980s, though the dating is not settled.
